question: If the sum of lower and upper quartiles is 6 and quartile deviation is 1.5, then the value of coefficient of quartile deviation is
solution:
The correct answer is **0.5**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **quartile deviation **is given by Q=((Q3-Q1))/(2), In this sum Q=1.5, therefore ((Q3-Q1))/(2)=1.5 implies (Q3-Q1)=3
 
• The sum of quartile deviation is given by 6 which means (Q3+Q1)=6
 
• The coefficient of quartile deviation is given by (Q3-Q1)/(Q3 +Q1). Therefore the **coefficient **of quartile deviation in this sum is (3)/(6) = 0.5. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Mathematically speaking, the quartile deviation is equal to half of the difference between the upper and lower quartile. In this case, the quartile deviation can be represented by the symbol QD, where Q3 stands for the upper quartile__ and Q1 for the __lower quartile__. The Semi Interquartile range is another name for quartile deviation.
 
• The __Quartile Deviation__ is an easy technique to calculate a distribution's spread relative to a measure of its central tendency (usually the mean). As a result, it provides you with a general sense of the range in which the middle 50% of your sample data is located. 

**Hence, *the coefficient of quartile deviation is 0.5. ***
